summary: The narrator meets Barry Morton, a Guatemalan official-linked figure, who evasively discusses a foreign engineer named Gary from Vierzon and suggests local officials avoid investigating foul play against foreigners. The narrator leaves with more questions, noticing Morton's secretary wears a silver cat pendant resembling jaguar medallions the narrator remembers from Kevin and Rachel, which has a blank back. The excerpt closes with the narrator's thoughts turning to Steve, whom they have not seen in three and a half months.
one_line: The narrator presses Barry Morton about an engineer named Gary, then notices a jaguar-like pendant on his secretary and thinks of Steve.
key_facts: The narrator tells Barry Morton there was an engineer living in Vierzon named Gary.
Morton is fiddling with an ornate letter opener that has an onyx jaguar head on its handle.
Morton says the sovereign state of Guatemala definitely plays by its own rules.
Morton says lower-level officials have developed a consensus that sometimes it is better not to be too industrious when foreigners meet with foul play.
The narrator feels Barry Morton knows more than he is telling them.
Morton's secretary is described as a stout, fiftyish Ladino matron with defiantly black-dyed hair.
The secretary wears thick glasses with Zircon trim and a small silver pendant on her low-cut sweater.
The pendant is the silver face of a cat, most likely the local jaguar.
The narrator recalls similar medallions from Kevin and Rachel.
The back of the secretary's medallion is blank silver, with no engraving of lines and dots.
The narrator considers that the secretary may handle matters that never reach Barry Morton's desk.
The narrator has not seen Steve in three and a half months and wants to recapture the lost time.
